headline: High: Roo Code’s filesystem/network/browser privileges can turn Pipecat outputs into unsafe actions or leaks; prompt-injection risk is lower but shared-bus and MCP pathways remain.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pipecat can emit text over a shared bus and stdin/stdout, while Roo Code can consume workspace content and MCP outputs. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if Pipecat-generated text is treated as trusted input. The pair is not directly documented interacting, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Pipecat output is copied into Roo Code prompts or MCP inputs without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF Roo Code treats agent-generated text as instructions rather than data, malicious directives can be executed.
mitigations: Prefix all Pipecat outputs with a strict data-only wrapper.
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from shared bus messages.
Add a manual review step before Roo Code executes any instruction derived from Pipecat text.
Use separate workspaces or channels for agent-to-agent communication.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and parser hardening for inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pipecat touches audio, video, images, text, and conversation state, and has broad network egress to model APIs. Roo Code reads and writes workspace files and can send context to configured APIs/MCP servers. In a shared workspace, sensitive conversational or code data can flow from Pipecat into Roo Code and then out to third parties, creating a default exfiltration risk.
conditions: IF Pipecat stores conversation state or media in the same workspace Roo Code reads, leakage is possible.
IF Roo Code forwards workspace/context content to configured model APIs or MCP servers, sensitive data can leave the environment.
mitigations: Keep Pipecat and Roo Code in separate directories.
Turn off any automatic file ingestion in Roo Code for shared folders.
Restrict Roo Code model/API endpoints to approved tenants only.
Avoid placing audio/video transcripts in the workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention and workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pipecat supports shared-bus shared state across instances, while Roo Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses in a per-workspace model. If both operate on the same workspace or repo, concurrent writes and git mutations can race and corrupt state. The overlap is explicit in the profiles, so this is a high-confidence conflict.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or workspace, file and git conflicts can occur.
IF Pipecat instances share a bus while Roo Code edits the same files, race conditions can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Assign separate worktrees per agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git locks or a single-writer policy.
Keep shared-bus messages read-only for Roo Code.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking and conflict detection.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat can generate conversational text and media-derived outputs, and Roo Code can act on those outputs through code edits, shell, browser, or MCP tools. If Roo Code treats Pipecat output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect commits or actions. The pathway exists, but the profiles do not show fully automated downstream execution by default.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses Pipecat output as a source of truth without validation, mistakes propagate.
IF Pipecat emits hallucinated or stale content that Roo Code converts into code or shell actions, downstream errors can occur.
mitigations: Require a human approval step before Roo Code acts on Pipecat output.
Add source verification for any facts extracted from Pipecat.
Limit Roo Code to read-only analysis when consuming Pipecat messages.
Log and diff all generated changes before execution.
requires-engineering: implement structured handoff schemas with validation.

E_compliance.rationale: Pipecat explicitly handles audio, video, images, text, and conversation state, while Roo Code handles source code and browser screenshots and may send data to external model APIs. If regulated conversational or media data is routed into Roo Code’s external APIs, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify certifications, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated audio or text from Pipecat is processed by Roo Code’s external model APIs, compliance obligations may differ.
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees, the pair may violate them without extra controls.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through Roo Code APIs.
Review vendor retention settings before enabling the pair.
Separate compliant and non-compliant data flows.
Document data-class handling for both agents.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency, retention, and deletion.
